citation: Høeg LD, Sjøberg KA, Jeppesen J, et al. Lipid-Induced Insulin Resistance Affects Women Less Than Men and Is Not Accompanied by Inflammation or Impaired Proximal Insulin Signaling. Diabetes. 2011.
protocol: Two trials (random order): 7 h Intralipid (20%) plus heparin or saline, with a euglycaemic hyperinsulinaemic clamp (1.42 mU/kg/min) during the last hours; after 8 days of controlled diet
population: n=16 (8 W, 8 M) healthy, age 25+/-1 y, BMI 21.5 (W) and 23.5 (M), VO2peak 47.3 and 52.3 mL/kg/min

reports.where: Table 2 (arterial, preclamp and clamp, by trial and sex)

note: Saline arm = plain overnight-fasted clamp; Intralipid arm = lipid-induced resistance (outside pulse's inputs unless FFA is clamped). Sex split.
